note: Installing an asset in a root must trash the asset already there. Vaporframe Fabricator leaves both in the root, so it is never trashed and Restore finds nothing
Egret installs only on a rezzed ice. The engine offers an unrezzed ice as its host

Dhegdheer can host any other program, but the engine never offers it for Leprechaun (a daemon), so the discount and the memory are wrong; the credit left after Atman is 1 short for the same reason. (Atman's spend is a choice since RF-1b, CR 9.6.9c.)
The Corp may install in a new remote server. IP Enforcement offers only existing remotes and stops with an error when there is none, after the tags are removed
The Corp may spend credits on a trace. The trace on Burke Bugs resolves at once at strength 0 with no chance to spend, as most traces do
X may be 0. Psychographics offers 1 to 3 only

The Corp chooses where the ice found by Tucana is installed; the engine always uses the server Tucana is in. The ice is also marked rezzed without its when-rezzed ability, so Logjam gets no counter (CR 8.5.15, 8.1.2e)
Takings of the same basic action are the same action. Jeeves Model Bioroids counts clicks inside one action only, so it never gives a click for three plays, draws or credits
Oaktown Renovation installs only faceup. Mushin No Shin installs it facedown
Gang Sign's breach of HQ happens when the agenda is scored, with no run needed. The engine puts it off until a run begins, so Archangel is never accessed or encountered.
Gordian Blade's strength ability has no Interface flag, so it can be used in the approach window. The card model flags it as interface and offers it only in an encounter.
Same missing breach as 3.4.4a.ex1: Gang Sign's breach is put off until a run begins, so there is no encounter outside a run for Gordian Blade's increase to last through.
Corroder's strength ability has no Interface flag, so it can be used outside an encounter and then lasts until the next checkpoint. The card model offers it only in an encounter.
Corroder's strength ability can be used in the approach window (step 6.9.2b). The card model offers it only in an encounter.
Trashing Warroid Tracker meets its own trigger condition, and the ability stays active until it resolves. The engine looks for it in the root after the trash and finds nothing, so no trace happens.

The Corp makes one mandatory draw. With Daily Business Show's choice open the engine stays at the mandatory-draw step and draws again on every pass, and it does not hold Daily Business Show to the first draw of the turn.

A move to the outermost position of a server with ice puts the run in the Approach Ice Phase for that ice. After Mirāju's move the engine carries on toward the server, so Mirāju is never approached again.

An ability that triggers when its card is accessed is active even while the card is inactive. With no run in progress the engine treats Ganked! in HQ as inactive and drops its ability, so no encounter happens.

Unleash lets the Corp resolve a subroutine of the ice it rezzed; the barrier subroutine gains 1 credit and its end-the-run does nothing. After Lycian Multi-Munition's subtype choice the engine never offers the subroutine.
After a forced encounter the game returns to the effect that caused it. After Shiro's nested breach and the encounter with Chrysalis the engine ends the whole run, so HQ is never reached.
When the run has moved to a server Because I Can could not have run, its 'If successful' effect does not apply and the breach is normal. The engine skips the breach of Archives altogether.
The choice between breaching and Account Siphon's effect is made when the breach would begin, after Ash's trace. The engine asks for it when the run is declared successful, before the trace.

A reaction window open when the run is ended is completed normally, so Formicary can still be rezzed and moved. The engine models Formicary as a paid ability and never offers it once the run has ended.
The Runner breaches the attacked server whether or not the run was declared successful. Under Crisium Grid the engine skips the breach.
The Corp chooses the server a card is installed in. Poétrï's install always makes a new remote server and asks nothing.

Hades Shard's [trash] is now open in every paid ability window (PF-S3c), so it is used and Hedge Fund leaves the game. breach_archives then turns the run into a run on Archives instead of breaching Archives now, so the run's own breach of its server never happens.

After a card has been accessed under Hudson 1.0's effect no other card can be accessed. The engine models the effect as a random access limit and lets the Runner access the newly trashed Wall of Static too.
Having accessed a card under Hudson 1.0's effect, the Runner has no candidates left. The engine still offers the Wall of Static in Archives.
The Runner breaches the attacked server whether or not the run was declared successful. Under Flagship the engine skips the breach, as it does under Crisium Grid.
After Otoroshi's access the Runner still breaches HQ and may access Flagship. Under Flagship the engine skips the breach.
With Flagship hosted on Cupellation its restriction ends and 2 cards from HQ become candidates. Under Flagship the engine skips the breach.

Strongbox's click is now charged (PF-S3b), but Seidr Laboratories still does not put PAD Campaign on top of R&D, so the Runner accesses Enigma instead of PAD Campaign. (The random access limit part, CR 7.3.5, was fixed by FX-access.)
When installing a program the Runner may first trash any number of installed programs. The engine offers this only when the memory limit would be exceeded, so Harbinger cannot be trashed this way.
The Corp makes one mandatory draw. After the Raman Rai and Daily Business Show sequence of the example the engine is still at the mandatory-draw step and draws again on every pass until R&D is empty.

A card found to be installed must be one the player can install, and its install cost is paid. Artist Colony offers Femme Fatale to a Runner with 2 credits and installs Corroder without charging its cost.
The card swapped in becomes installed, which meets A Teia's condition at the next checkpoint. The engine never offers A Teia's install after Tatu-Bola's swap.

Kitsune's subroutine breaches HQ while it resolves, and the run then goes on to its own breach of Archives. The engine moves the attacked server to HQ and puts the breach off to the Success Phase, so Archives is never breached.
The Runner declares whether a card that entered the root during the breach becomes a candidate. The engine asks nothing and makes it one.
The Runner may declare that a card that entered the root during the breach does not become a candidate. The engine asks nothing and the card is accessed.

Punitive Counterstrike counts the agendas stolen in the Runner's turn that just ended, and The Cleaners adds 1. The engine rolls the stolen points only when the Runner's turn begins, so on the Corp's turn X is 0.

The reader expected the grip to keep its 4 cards because the Runner is flatlined at once. The CR does not say so: suffering damage is trashing cards, and 'immediately' means the game ends before I've Had Worse can resolve. The expectation on the grip was dropped.
In a trace the Corp may spend credits to raise the trace strength. The trace on Gemini's subroutine resolves at once with no chance to spend, so the Corp cannot reach strength 5.
In a trace the Corp and then the Runner may spend credits. The trace on Gemini's subroutine resolves at once, so neither can.

Skorpios Defense Systems lets the Corp remove 1 of the cards being trashed together. The engine offers only one of the three cards trashed by the damage (a Sure Gamble), so I've Had Worse cannot be removed. It goes to the heap, and the 3 cards its ability draws are left in the set-aside zone and never reach the grip

A card ability can tell the Runner to breach a server directly. Gang Sign says 'Whenever the Corp scores an agenda, breach HQ.' The engine puts the breach off until a run begins, so the encounter outside a run that CR 9.6.13d's example needs never happens and Mayfly's 'when this run ends' rule goes untested

The Class Act's interrupt is relevant to any instruction expected to draw cards. The engine does not offer it for the basic action to draw a card (it does for a draw from a card ability), so the top card is drawn with no look

An interrupt window opens whenever an instruction becomes imminent. The engine gives Casting Call's 2 tags with no window, so Decoy cannot be used, Thunder Art Gallery never triggers and the example's point (No One Home is not pending) is not reached
A paid ability interrupt need not have been active when the window opened. The engine gives Casting Call's 2 tags with no interrupt window at all, so neither Decoy can be used

In an interrupt window the active player has priority first, and The Cleaners' printed ability is a conditional interrupt the Corp uses when it has priority. The engine applies its +1 as the window opens, so the damage is 3, two Plascrete Carapace counters leave 1, Guru Davinder then prevents 1 and its second ability triggers. By the example the Runner removes the damage first and Guru Davinder stays

The driver's mistake, not the expectation's: it looked for a reveal in the engine's list of reveals. The engine shows the Corp the grip through the choice it opens for the Runner, which both seats see. The driver now reads the Corp's own view and the case agrees; the expectation is unchanged
Prāna Condenser's ability trashes it as a cost and then counts its hosted power counters, which are set aside as the cost is paid. The engine does no damage: the counters go with the card

The click to play an event is paid before its play abilities resolve, so Ritual's 'for each click you have remaining' counts 3 when it is played as the first click of four. The engine counts the clicks the Runner had when the play began and draws 4. (The Class Act's single look, at one more card than is drawn, is right.)

NASX lets the Corp spend up to 2 credits each time it gains credits from another card's ability. After the 1 credit gained for Ice Wall the engine offers a spend of 1 only, with 6 credits in the pool. Both instances do resolve separately, as the example says
A 'must' cannot force a player to pay an additional cost they wish to decline. With Service Outage active the engine offers a Runner with Always Be Running only runs for the first click

The run is in progress when 'run begins' abilities resolve, so Cezve's credits can pay for Masterwork (v37)'s install. With 1 credit in the pool and 2 on Cezve the engine does not offer the install of a 3-credit Cyberfeeder at all; with 3 credits in the pool it does

With all 4 MU used and 0 credits in the pool, the engine's 'Install MKUltra from heap' does nothing: it never asks which program to trash and never counts Cezve's credits, so the legal install (trash another program, pay 2 from Cezve) cannot be made. The illegal one (trashing Cezve and paying with its credits) is not made either

Cookbook's and Tranquilizer's abilities meet their conditions together when Tranquilizer is installed, and the Runner picks the order. The engine resolves Tranquilizer's first and only then asks about Cookbook: nobody is asked for an order. The outcome of that order is right
As cookbook#1: the Runner cannot resolve Cookbook first, so Tranquilizer never sees 3 counters when it checks and the ice stays rezzed

Paying a cost cannot be changed or cancelled by an optional interrupt, and Funhouse's tag is a nested cost. The engine offers Decoy on that tag: the card data models Funhouse's "unless" like Data Raven's choice (CR 9.12.3d), so the tag is not marked as a cost. (The repeated "take 1 tag or end the run" question while Decoy was installed is fixed: the encounter ability is asked once.)

Spoilers and Longevity Serum both trigger when the agenda is scored; the Corp, as active player, resolves first and then Spoilers trashes the top card of R&D. When Longevity Serum opens its choice the engine never marks Spoilers pending, so nothing is trashed
Pinhole Threading replaces the breach with an access that is not a breach. The engine still gives Aumakua its 'finish breaching' counter

A forced encounter does not change the attacked server, and Border Control's ability can be used 'only during a run on this server'. During the encounter Ganked! forces, the run is still on HQ, but the engine also offers the ability of the Border Control protecting the remote server
Loup's ability triggers the first time each turn the Runner trashes a card they are accessing, by any means. The engine does not trigger it when Carnivore trashes the card: no credit, no draw

Seamless Launch places counters; it does not advance, so its target need not be a card the Corp can advance. The engine offers only agendas and cards that can be advanced: PAD Campaign is not a target and nothing is placed
As seamless-launch#1; the engine also looks only at the Corp's servers, so the Runner's installed Corroder is not a target

The ruling says Spin Doctor's ability cannot be used with nothing in Archives and only 1 card in R&D, because nothing would change. CR v26.03 has no rule that an ability must change the game state: a paid ability can be used whenever its cost is paid (9.5.2f), and 'up to 2' allows 0. The engine follows the CR and lets the Corp use it
An ability that lets a card be advanced is active while the card is unrezzed. The engine never offers to advance Urtica Cipher (its card data has no 'can be advanced' flag)

The position advances Urtica Cipher, which the engine cannot advance (see urtica-cipher#1), so the identity's 2 credits for a first advance are not reached here. CR 9.6.6a.ex1 covers the same ruling with Ice Wall and agrees
The position places Seamless Launch's counters on a PAD Campaign, which the engine does not offer as a target (see seamless-launch#1). The credits agree; the counters are not placed

The reader had the Runner prevent the tag with Decoy and Funhouse then end the run. Paying a cost cannot be changed by an optional interrupt (CR 1.16.1a), so Decoy cannot be used on a tag taken as a nested cost: the tag is taken and the run goes on. The expectation was corrected; the ruling’s answer (the Runner cannot keep the run by preventing the tag) agrees with it

Moved to the outermost position of Archives, the Runner's position is that ice and the step becomes the Approach Ice Phase. After Susanoo-no-Mikoto's subroutine the engine changes the attacked server to Archives but puts the Runner past the ice, in the window after an encounter: Ice Wall is never approached
As run-timing-redirection-updates-current-ice-5047: after Susanoo-no-Mikoto the Runner never approaches or encounters Ice Wall on Archives. Corroder's strength does return to 2

observations.engine: both kinds of run happened this turn

note: A run that reached the Success Phase is not declared unsuccessful. When a forced encounter during the breach ends the run, the engine also records an unsuccessful run

observations.engine: the steps cannot be finished: after equal bids Konjin's Psi Game starts again

note: With equal bids 'if the bids differ' is not met and Konjin's ability is over. The engine starts Konjin's encounter and its Psi Game again after equal bids, so the run never gets past Konjin and the breach with Ganked! is not reached
The CR treats an encounter with no run in progress as its own thing (6.1.4b, 6.5.9a). The engine builds a run for the encounter Quest Completed and Ganked! cause, so a run is in progress during it

observations.engine: both kinds of run happened this turn

note: With no run in progress 'End the run.' ends only the encounter. The engine records an unsuccessful run

During a forced encounter a move 'resolves and changes the parameters of the underlying run normally': Cell Portal puts the run in the Approach Ice Phase at Konjin (6.2.8b), so Konjin is approached and encountered again and starts a second Psi Game. The engine goes back into the first encounter with Konjin (its reminder text, which has no effect) and no second game starts. cr-checker notes a weaker reading, CR 6.2.7c's 'the run continues to the Movement Phase', under which Konjin is passed with no second game

observations.engine: the steps cannot be finished: after equal bids Konjin's Psi Game starts again

note: As forced-encounters-forced-encounters-during-run#c: after equal bids on the way in, the engine starts Konjin's Psi Game again, so the breach and the forced encounters inside it are not reached

The reader had Gordian Blade's '+1 strength for the remainder of this run' expire at once when used in an encounter with no run in progress (CR 9.10.4). CR 3.9.5c's example names this case: the increase lasts for that encounter. The expectation was corrected to 3 during the encounter and 2 after it, which the engine shows
